overview: Both can develop into other cell types, but stem cells are less committed and can self-renew indefinitely.
genZNote: Stem cells are undecided majors who can pick almost anything. Progenitor cells already picked a specific track.

aspects.label: Self-Renewal Capacity
aspects.valueA: Can divide indefinitely, maintaining a pool of undifferentiated cells.
aspects.valueB: Limited ability to self-renew; mostly moves toward differentiation.

aspects.label: Differentiation Potential
aspects.valueA: Can be totipotent, pluripotent, or multipotent, giving rise to many cell types.
aspects.valueB: More restricted (usually unipotent or bipotent) — committed toward one or two specific lineages.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Embryonic stem cells; haematopoietic stem cells in bone marrow.
aspects.valueB: Myeloid progenitor cells that will become specific blood cell types.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: All progenitor cells arise from stem cells, but not all stem cell divisions produce progenitor cells — some just make more stem cells.
overlay.memoryTrick: Stem cells = flexible and renewable. Progenitor = already committed, closer to the final cell type.
overlay.commonMisconception: Progenitor cells are not the same as stem cells — they have already lost the indefinite self-renewal ability that defines a true stem cell.
